stories.headline: Form 3CEB transfer pricing report due 31 October
points: Form 3CEB is for anyone with an international or specified domestic transaction in the relevant previous year.
A chartered accountant must submit the report by the deadline, or the assessing officer may impose a ₹1,00,000 penalty.
Filing is on the income tax portal: taxpayer assigns a CA, CA fills the form, taxpayer approves it. ITR is due 30 November.
stories.why_it_matters: CAs certify transfer pricing documentation under Section 92E, so deadlines, penalties and portal workflow are core practice knowledge.
stories.source_title: Income Tax Form 3CEB deadline today: Who must file transfer pricing report by 31 Oct and how to submit it? | Explained

stories.headline: Delhi HC: Section 270A penalty fails if notice lacks specific charge
points: Delhi HC dismissed the Revenue's appeal against a Tribunal order that cancelled a Section 270A penalty for AY 2017-18.
Notices spoke of under-reporting, but the 200% penalty was imposed for misreporting, with no matching show-cause notice.
Court said the missing specific charge was clear from the record and found no reason to interfere with the Tribunal.
stories.why_it_matters: Shows that penalty notices must name the exact charge under Section 270A, a key point in tax litigation and natural justice.
stories.source_title: Income Tax | Section 270A Penalty Invalid Without Specific Charge in Notice: Delhi HC

stories.headline: TCS paid on a car costing over ₹10 lakh can be claimed in your ITR
points: Dealers collect 1% TCS when a motor vehicle's sale value is above ₹10 lakh, to help the tax department track big purchases.
The TCS is advance tax deposited against the buyer's PAN; on a ₹20 lakh car it would be about ₹20,000.
Buyers need Form 27D, must check the TCS in Form 26AS or AIS, then claim it in the ITR; any excess is refunded.
stories.why_it_matters: TCS credit, Form 26AS/AIS matching and ITR claims are everyday topics in income tax practice and exam questions.
stories.source_title: Buying a car on Dhanteras, Diwali 2026? You could get at least ₹10,000 as tax refund next year — here's how
check_notes: The 'Why it matters' line says TCS credit, Form 26AS/AIS matching and ITR claims are 'everyday topics in income tax practice and exam questions'. The source never mentions income tax practice or exams; this is the editor's own framing, not something the source reports.
Point 2 calls the TCS 'advance tax'. The source's wording is 'tax paid in advance', which is not the same as the formal term advance tax. This is a small wording change.
